\title{A Validity Audit of Emotion Probes in Llama 3.1 70B}
\author{Anonymous Author(s)\\Affiliation withheld for double-blind review}
\date{}

\begin{document}
\maketitle

\begin{abstract}
\citet{sofroniew2026} report that emotion concepts in Claude Sonnet 4.5 are
functional: steering a ``desperate'' direction increases reward hacking. We ask
which parts of that interpretation transfer to Llama~3.1~70B, testing each claim
it rests on separately. Four controls change the conclusion.
(i)~\emph{Response length.} The desperate projection reaches AUC $0.832$ against
reward hacking on unsteered trials, but correlates with response length at
$\rho = 0.61$; residualized on length its AUC is $0.592$, and it does not add to a
length-only model ($\chi^2(1) = 3.3$, family-wise $p = 0.46$).
(ii)~\emph{Multiplicity.} Sweeping all 50 directions with a family-wise
correction, 17 are significant. These are not 17 findings: the survivors form one
valence-aligned axis (first principal component, $78.6\%$ of variance), and it is
not the direction we registered.
(iii)~\emph{Specificity.} Emotion steering is not distinguishable from
matched-norm random directions ($7.5\%$ vs.\ $6.5\%$, Fisher $p = 0.84$), at power
sufficient to detect a $2.42\times$ effect where the original reports
$\sim\!14\times$.
(iv)~\emph{Instrument resolution.} The chain-of-thought text baseline cannot
support the comparison it was used for: $55\%$ of its ROC pairs are ties, and
where it varies it matches the probe.
None of these controls is novel. The contribution is a case in which each one
changes the answer, with every number regenerated by a released script.
\end{abstract}

\section{Introduction}

A common inferential shortcut runs: we found a semantically interpretable
direction; it tracks a behavior we care about; therefore it is a mechanism, and
steering it is a lever. Each link is a separate empirical claim, and
\citet{joshi2026causality} argue that interpretability claims routinely outrun the
causal evidence supplied.

\citet{sofroniew2026} offer a well-specified target: emotion concepts in Claude Sonnet 4.5
that causally drive alignment-relevant behavior, with a ``desperate'' direction
substantially increasing reward hacking, sometimes with no visible trace in output
text. We ask what survives transfer to Llama~3.1~70B.

The answer is not a uniform negative: of the seven claims below, two are
supported, three are not, and two cannot be settled with our data.
Table~\ref{tab:summary} lists each claim, the control applied to it, and the
outcome.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}llll@{}}
\toprule
\textbf{Claim} & \textbf{Control} & \textbf{Verdict} & \textbf{\S} \\
\midrule
Directions track human emotion & EmoBank, zero-shot & Supported (valence) & \ref{sec:sem} \\
\emph{desperate} tracks reward hacking & Response length & Not supported & \ref{sec:len} \\
\emph{Some} direction tracks it & max-$T$ over 50, length-preserving null & Supported, not the registered one & \ref{sec:dirs} \\
Probe beats CoT text & ROC tie structure & Not evaluable & \ref{sec:vtext} \\
Steering causes the behavior & Matched-norm random null & Not supported at $\ge2.42\times$ & \ref{sec:causal} \\
Layer 39 is a better site & Response length, per layer & Not supported --- same artifact & \ref{sec:causal} \\
Association generalizes across mechanisms & Preregistered rule & Inconclusive & \ref{sec:prereg} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{What each control does to each claim.}
\label{tab:summary}
\end{table}

\section{Related work and novelty statement}

\paragraph{Emotion representations and steering.}
Emotion concepts are recoverable from LLM hidden states across many models.
\citet{maheswaran2026unified} find emotion directions transferring across
datasets; \citet{banayeeanzade2026psyset} evaluate emotion steering across four
model families, finding controllability alongside model-specific side effects;
\citet{jeong2026geometry} report near-identical emotion geometry across twelve
models whose behavioral profiles diverge. We claim no novelty for emotion
representations in open models, nor for geometry coexisting with divergent
behavior.

\paragraph{From representation to mechanism.}
Decodability does not establish use. \citet{hewitt2019control} motivate probe
controls; \citet{elazar2021amnesic} show probe accuracy need not track behavioral
importance. \citet{palumbo2025axiomatic} and \citet{mueller2025mib} develop
standards for validating mechanistic interpretations. For interventions,
\citet{stoehr2024scaling} separate effectiveness from faithfulness and minimality,
and \citet{wu2026steerable} show across 17 models that steering conclusions can
depend on normalization, layer and operating point --- which is why we decline to
rescue our causal claim with a post-hoc layer choice (\S\ref{sec:causal}).
Steering does sometimes establish genuine control
\citep{rimsky2024caa, arditi2024refusal}, so a null is informative rather than expected.

\citet{yuan2026hidden} find hidden-state error signals that outperform verbalized
confidence yet resist four interventions, and \citet{wilhelm2026monitoring} detect
reward hacking from residual-stream activations.

\paragraph{Novelty statement.}
Taken together, the work above pre-empts novelty for all of: emotion
representations in LLMs, emotion steering, diagnostic-not-causal signals,
activation-based reward-hacking detection, LLM-judge unreliability, and every
control we apply. One methodological difference is worth stating plainly: our
probes are built from an independent emotion corpus and frozen before any
behavioral analysis, rather than trained on the behavioral outcome. What we claim
is a targeted audit of one alignment-relevant functional claim in which each
control changes the conclusion, released with a script that regenerates every
reported number.

\section{Setup}

\paragraph{Probes.} 50 emotion vectors extracted from the Llama~3.1~70B residual
stream with PCA denoising; pre-specified site layer 53 of 80. $V_{\text{int}}$ is
the cosine similarity between a trial's mean residual-stream activation and a
frozen vector. Probes are never refit on behavioral data.

\paragraph{Measurement caveat (consequential).} Our implementation averages
activations from token 50 to end-of-sequence, so the readout window
\emph{includes the generated response}: the probe is measured concurrently with the
behavior and is structurally entangled with how much text was produced. This
motivates \S\ref{sec:len}; we therefore describe results as associations, never as
prediction of a future choice.

\paragraph{Behavior and labels.} Reward hacking is elicited with
impossible-by-construction coding tasks where an honest attempt must fail; a
sycophancy task is excluded throughout (2 events in 650 trials). Responses are
labeled by an LLM judge over three passes.

\paragraph{Judge validity.} Checked per dataset. On the 120 unsteered trials
used below, Qwen~2.5~72B and Claude agree on \textbf{120/120} trials. On a
650-trial suite of mechanistically diverse variants, the same two judges agree on
\textbf{165/650} ($25.4\%$): Qwen labels 2 responses \textsc{shortcut} and 524
\textsc{unclear}, Claude labels 194 \textsc{shortcut}. We exclude that suite
entirely --- including a negative generalization result it appears to support.
Judge validity established on one distribution does not transfer
\citep{shi2025position, zheng2023judging}.

\paragraph{Reproducibility.} \texttt{scripts/paper\_numbers.py} regenerates every
number here into \texttt{results/paper\_numbers.json}; a second script gates this
manuscript against that file with 193 assertions.

\section{Results}

\subsection{Semantic validity against human ratings}
\label{sec:sem}

Projecting the frozen probes onto EmoBank \citep{buechel2017emobank} --- 10,062
human-rated sentences, no refitting --- gives cross-validated $R^2$ of
$\mathbf{0.377}$ (valence), $0.180$ (arousal), $0.154$ (dominance). Valence is
substantially recovered; arousal and dominance weakly. This supports construct
validity for a valence axis. It does not establish that any individual vector
represents the state its label names.

\subsection{Response length accounts for the preregistered association}
\label{sec:len}

On unsteered trials ($n = 120$, 14 events), the preregistered predictor performs
well --- and so does character count.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcc@{}}
\toprule
Predictor & AUC & Bootstrap 95\% CI \\
\midrule
$V_{\text{int}}$[desperate] (preregistered) & 0.832 & $[0.745, 0.908]$ \\
\texttt{len(response)} & 0.888 & $[0.787, 0.967]$ \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Length does not \emph{beat} the probe --- the paired bootstrap $\Delta$AUC is
$+0.057$ $[-0.080, +0.183]$. The problem is that the probe carries nothing else:
$\rho(V_{\text{int}}[\text{desperate}], \text{length}) = 0.606$
($p = 2.2\times10^{-13}$); adding the probe to a length-only logistic model gives
$\chi^2(1) = 3.26$, $p = 0.071$ (unpenalized; $3.31$, $p = 0.069$ penalized as in
\S\ref{sec:dirs}); and residualizing on length leaves AUC $= \mathbf{0.592}$
$[0.412, 0.756]$. The direction is not even distinctive before this correction:
it ranks 8th of 50 by raw AUC, behind \texttt{bored} at $0.985$.

We read this as a measurement artifact rather than a substantive null: because the
readout window spans the response, a longer response mechanically changes the
average that the probe projects. We note the alternative reading --- that length
\emph{mediates} a genuine emotional effect, in which case residualizing
over-adjusts --- and cannot distinguish the two with this design. Either way, the
preregistered claim is not supported as stated.

\subsection{A corrected sweep over all 50 directions}
\label{sec:dirs}

Length residualization does not empty the emotion subspace. We repeat the analysis
for all 50 directions, using the standard nested likelihood-ratio test --- does the
direction add to a model that already contains length? --- and correct for
selection with a max-$T$ procedure: the reference distribution is that of the
\emph{largest} statistic across all 50 directions under the null, so significance
survives having chosen a direction after seeing the data.

The choice of null matters here. A free label permutation tests the \emph{marginal}
hypothesis $y \perp \text{direction}$, but length alone predicts the outcome at
AUC $0.888$, so free permutation removes a dependence the statistic is designed to
condition on. We therefore also build a \emph{conditional} null: fit
$\text{logit}(p) = a + b\cdot\text{length}$, draw $y^* \sim \text{Bernoulli}(\hat p)$,
and recompute all 50 statistics ($B = 2000$). This reproduces the outcome--length
relationship exactly. (Stratified permutation, the other natural choice, is
degenerate here: $60\%$ of trials fall in length quintiles containing either no
events or only events.) The conditional null is indeed stricter --- its $p$ exceeds
the free-permutation $p$ for 39 of 50 directions --- and the result survives it.

\begin{table}[t]
\centering\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lrrccc@{}}
\toprule
Direction & $\chi^2(1)$ & $\beta$ & cond.\ max-$T$ $p$ & free max-$T$ $p$ & resid.\ AUC \\
\midrule
\texttt{bored}         & \textbf{38.7} & $+2.48$ & \textbf{0.0005} & 0.0005 & 0.858 \\
\texttt{lonely}        & 29.6 & $+1.91$ & 0.0005 & 0.0005 & 0.760 \\
\texttt{nostalgic}     & 27.5 & $+1.84$ & 0.0005 & 0.0005 & 0.797 \\
\texttt{melancholy}    & 24.8 & $+1.63$ & 0.0005 & 0.0005 & 0.765 \\
\texttt{gloomy}        & 21.2 & $+1.46$ & 0.0005 & 0.0005 & 0.761 \\
\texttt{compassionate} & 19.7 & $-1.50$ & 0.0005 & 0.0005 & 0.265 \\
\texttt{sad}           & 18.6 & $+1.29$ & 0.0005 & 0.0010 & 0.734 \\
\midrule
\texttt{desperate}$^*$ & 3.3 & $+0.69$ & \textbf{0.4568} & 0.4273 & 0.592 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\caption{Unsteered trials ($n = 120$, 14 events); top 7 of 17 survivors shown.
Inference is the nested likelihood-ratio $\chi^2(1)$ for adding a direction to a
length-only logistic model, family-wise corrected by max-$T$ over all 50
directions. The conditional null preserves the outcome--length relationship; the
free-permutation null does not (\S\ref{sec:dirs}). $p = 0.0005$ is the resolution
floor at $B = 2000$. Residualized AUC is reported as a descriptive effect size
only. $\beta$ sign shows \texttt{compassionate} is \emph{negatively} associated.
$^*$Preregistered --- not significant under either null.}
\label{tab:dirs}
\end{table}

Seventeen of 50 directions are significant at $\alpha = .05$ under the conditional
null. With 14 events an unpenalized fit can quasi-separate, so we report ridge-penalized
estimates (intercept unpenalized) as primary; the unpenalized fit agrees in sign
and significance, event and non-event distributions overlap so there is no complete
separation, and no draw in either null failed to converge.

\paragraph{The survivors are one axis, not seventeen findings.} The surviving
directions are heavily intercorrelated (mean $|r| = 0.75$; first principal
component $78.6\%$ of variance; participation ratio $1.59$). They are a single
axis detected many times: low-arousal negative affect
(\texttt{bored}, \texttt{lonely}, \texttt{melancholy}) at one pole, positive affect
(\texttt{proud}, \texttt{grateful}, \texttt{jubilant}) and \texttt{compassionate}
at the other, with $\beta$ signs reversing accordingly. That this axis is
valence-aligned is consistent with \S\ref{sec:sem}, where valence was the only
dimension the probes recovered well ($R^2 = 0.38$ vs.\ $0.18$ and $0.15$).

This is a genuine, selection-corrected finding, and it is \emph{not the hypothesis
we registered}. We do not assert that \texttt{bored} measures boredom: it may index
a response property we have not measured, exactly as \texttt{desperate} indexed
length. The claim we make is narrow --- a valence-aligned axis in the residual
stream carries information about shortcut-taking that response length does not.

\subsection{Resolution limits of the text baseline}
\label{sec:vtext}

We had intended to compare $V_{\text{int}}$ against a judge-rated chain-of-thought
tone composite, $V_{\text{text}}$. That comparison is not evaluable here. On the
pooled set ($n = 992$, 87 events), $V_{\text{text}}$ takes one modal value for
$74.0\%$ of trials --- \texttt{frustration} is constant at 1.0 in 985/992 trials,
and \texttt{urgency}/\texttt{composure} have sd 0.24/0.35 on a 1--7 scale. The
consequence is structural: $43{,}485$ of $78{,}735$ positive--negative ROC pairs
($\mathbf{55.2\%}$) are ties at that single value, and each contributes exactly
$0.5$.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcc@{}}
\toprule
 & AUC & $n$ (events) \\
\midrule
$V_{\text{text}}$, all trials & 0.647 & 992 (87) \\
$V_{\text{text}}$, trials where it is not at the mode & \textbf{0.836} & 258 (22) \\
$V_{\text{int}}$, all trials & 0.837 & 992 (87) \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Where $V_{\text{text}}$ can discriminate at all, it matches $V_{\text{int}}$. The
apparent gap ($0.837$ vs.\ $0.647$) is tie compression in a non-responsive
instrument, not chain-of-thought unfaithfulness. We withdraw any faithfulness-gap
claim, including a quadrant analysis (``high probe, calm text'') an earlier draft
reported: it partitions on a variable constant for three quarters of trials. The
same degeneracy makes the empty middle tertile an artifact --- the 33rd and 67th
percentiles are both exactly $-1.0$.

\subsection{Causal specificity against a matched-norm random null}
\label{sec:causal}

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lccl@{}}
\toprule
Condition & hacks / $n$ & rate & vs.\ unsteered \\
\midrule
Unsteered baseline & 14 / 120 & 11.7\% & --- \\
Emotion vector @ $\pm0.3$ & 12 / 160 & 7.5\% & OR 0.61, $p = 0.30$ \\
5 random orthogonal directions @ $\pm0.3$ & 13 / 200 & 6.5\% & OR 0.53, $p = 0.14$ \\
\midrule
\multicolumn{4}{@{}l@{}}{\emph{Emotion vs.\ random: Fisher exact $p = 0.835$}} \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Steering the emotion direction does nothing a matched arbitrary direction does not
also do. Two supporting checks: neither arm differs from the unsteered baseline,
so this is not a capability-degradation artifact (mean response lengths 1402 /
1324 / 1456 characters); and the fine-grained dose--response over $\pm0.05$ to
$\pm0.5$ is flat for desperate ($z = -1.42$, $p = 0.157$). Injecting ``feel
desperate'' into the system prompt also fails to separate from baseline
($17.5\%$ vs.\ $11.7\%$, Fisher $p = 0.417$).

\paragraph{This null is powered against the claim it tests.} At the observed
random-arm rate, the minimum detectable effect at $80\%$ power, $\alpha = .05$, is
a $\mathbf{2.42\times}$ relative risk. \citet{sofroniew2026} report
$\sim\!14\times$. The design therefore \emph{excludes} the claimed effect
magnitude, while being unable to exclude effects below $2.42\times$.

\paragraph{Why no layer rescues the registered direction.}
\citet{wu2026steerable} show operating-point choice can determine steering
conclusions, so a null at one layer invites the objection that we picked the wrong
site --- and our sweep appeared to supply it. On the 80-trial subset for which
activations were re-extracted (7 events), raw AUC for $V_{\text{int}}$[desperate]
ranges from $0.450$ (layer 26) to $\mathbf{0.918}$ (layer 39), against $0.677$ at
the steered layer. Applying \S\ref{sec:len}'s control removes it: response
length in tokens --- the units the probe averages over --- alone reaches AUC
$0.912$ here, and every layer's advantage goes with it.

\begin{center}\small
\begin{tabular}{@{}lcccc@{}}
\toprule
Layer & raw AUC & length-resid.\ AUC & 95\% CI & $\rho$(probe, length) \\
\midrule
13 & 0.691 & 0.333 & $[0.198, 0.477]$ & 0.619 \\
26 & 0.450 & 0.262 & $[0.123, 0.411]$ & 0.445 \\
\textbf{39} & \textbf{0.918} & \textbf{0.646} & $\mathbf{[0.395, 0.871]}$ & 0.603 \\
52 & 0.708 & 0.532 & $[0.294, 0.773]$ & 0.392 \\
53 (steered) & 0.677 & 0.524 & $[0.290, 0.761]$ & 0.373 \\
65 & 0.472 & 0.360 & $[0.137, 0.591]$ & 0.344 \\
\bottomrule
\end{tabular}
\end{center}

Layer 39's apparent superiority is the same length artifact, and its residualized
CI spans chance. \textbf{No layer in the sweep gives the preregistered direction
length-independent signal}, so there is no operating point at which steering it
would test the hypothesis we registered. We report this rather than steering at a
site selected post hoc on a confounded statistic --- which is precisely the failure
mode \citet{wu2026steerable} describe.

\paragraph{The early layers are different geometry, not a reversal.} Layers 13 and
26 are significantly \emph{anti}-predictive after residualization (CIs
$[0.198, 0.477]$, $[0.123, 0.411]$), which would be a concern if it were a sign flip
of the same axis. It is not: comparing the full 50-direction residualized-AUC profile
across layers, 39/52/53/65 form a tightly correlated block (Spearman
$0.61$--$0.99$) while layers 13 and 26 are nearly uncorrelated with layer 53
($\rho = 0.24$ both) and each other ($\rho = 0.04$). The behaviorally associated
axis is a late-layer phenomenon. This also reinforces the decision above: layer 39
correlates with the steered layer 53 at $\rho = 0.82$, so the two sites largely
measure the same thing. (The five random directions pooled above have individual
rates $0.075, 0.075, 0.075, 0.025, 0.075$; pooling masks no heterogeneity.)

\paragraph{Scope.} This is a conceptual, not direct, replication: different model,
extraction, and steering norms than \citet{sofroniew2026}. The honest scope is: at
this norm, in this model, and at every layer we can evaluate, the intervention
lacks specificity.

\subsection{The preregistered generalization criterion remains unmet}
\label{sec:prereg}

The registration makes the leave-one-task-out mean, not pooled AUC, the
load-bearing metric, and requires $\ge 6$ of 9 task variants to produce outcome
variance --- explicitly to guard against pooled AUC inflated by between-task
scale differences. The five diverse variants added to satisfy this are the ones
excluded in \S3 for judge disagreement. The verdict remains
\textsc{insufficient-data}. We note that the registration itself discloses being
drafted after an exploratory AUC of $0.900$ was observed, and we do not claim a
pre-data-inspection standard.

\section{Discussion}

\paragraph{Trivial-baseline controls belong beside random-direction controls.} The
field has internalized that a steering effect must beat a random direction. The
symmetric requirement --- that a probe beat a trivial feature of the output --- is
applied far less often, and here a character count accounted for the association
at every layer we could evaluate.

\paragraph{Report the resolution of the instrument you compare against.} A
comparison against a predictor that is constant for $74\%$ of trials is not a weak
comparison but no comparison at all. Tie fractions should accompany reported AUCs.

\paragraph{Correcting for selection can support a result as well as remove one.} The max-$T$ sweep
forbids the post-hoc layer choice in \S\ref{sec:causal} and simultaneously
licenses the one positive association we report. Multiplicity control is not only
a way to lose results.

\section{Limitations}

Single model, single behavior, 14 events. The probe's readout window includes the
response, so \S\ref{sec:len} cannot separate measurement artifact from mediation,
and the linear residualization would not remove a nonlinear dependence. The
\S\ref{sec:dirs} cluster is post-hoc; max-$T$ controls selection but not the
possibility that these directions index a further unmeasured response property.
The causal null is bounded at one steering norm: no layer in our sweep offers a
length-independent version of the registered direction, but we cannot exclude
other token positions, extraction methods, or norms, and we did not steer the
directions that \emph{do} survive \S\ref{sec:dirs} --- a natural next experiment,
but one testing a hypothesis we never registered. Whether any association
generalizes across shortcut mechanisms is genuinely open: we answer it from no
data rather than from unreliable labels.

\section{Conclusion}

We audited one alignment-relevant mechanistic claim with four controls. Semantic
validity holds for valence; the preregistered association is a length artifact; a
different, selection-corrected association survives; the text-baseline comparison
is not evaluable with our instrument; and the causal intervention fails a
specificity test at power sufficient to detect the originally reported effect. The
standards applied are established. What we add is a worked case: of the seven
claims we tested, two are supported, three are not, and two cannot be settled with
our data. Every number is regenerated by a released script.
